Internal: the SPSS-style codes a column's markers take in jconvert()

Source: R/missing-internals.R
dot-jst_spss_marker_plan.Rd

The Stata-to-SPSS mapping of jconvert(to = "spss"), in one place (Session 361): a column's markers, sorted, take the convention codes in letter order (.jst_tag_letters_to_codes()); a column with more markers than codes takes a missing-value RANGE instead (Session 319), starting at the first code and running one integer per marker in the direction the codes run, from the first toward the second. A single code gives no direction, and a range that would reach or cross zero is refused. jconvert()'s pre-flight builds its plan here, and the SPSS-to-Stata branch asks it what the trip back would give (the return-trip note, the S354 item), so the two cannot disagree.

Usage

.jst_spss_marker_plan(tags, convention_codes)

Arguments

tags

Character vector of the column's distinct lowercase marker letters, sorted.

convention_codes

The missing.convention.codes setting.

Value

A list: plan, a numeric vector of codes named by letter (the mappable subset when refused); band, the range's two ends or NULL; refused, TRUE when the markers outnumber the codes and no range can be formed.
